title: Let a cheap check decide whether the expensive model runs at all
contract: Four mechanisms, all at $0: `--no-agent` script jobs (script IS the job, stdout delivered verbatim, empty stdout = silence — the classic watchdog); script-as-context (script runs first, stdout injected as `## Script Output`, empty output skips the AI call entirely); the wake gate, where the last stdout line `{"wakeAgent": false}` suppresses the LLM and the delivery, fail-open on anything unparseable; and monitor mode, where a script or URL is hashed byte-exactly and an unchanged tick suppresses the run while a change injects a unified diff — with the new hash persisted at detection time so a failed agent run cannot re-alert forever. title: A recurring wakeup inside the conversation you are already having
contract: `/loop [interval] <prompt> [--times N] [--until <cond>]` with status/pause/resume/stop, persisted per session in SessionDB so `/resume` restores it. The gateway idle watcher scans persisted loops every 15 s and skips (leaving the tick due) when a turn is running, when a goal owns the boundary, or when there is no route. contract: Three barrier kinds on the goal state — wait on a pid until the process exits, wait on a registered session until its own trigger fires, wait until a wall-clock deadline — and while any is active `evaluate_after_turn` short-circuits **without burning a turn or calling the judge**. The judge sees the live background-process list and can itself return a third verdict, `wait`. Any dead pid, fired trigger or elapsed deadline clears the barrier on the next check, so a stale barrier can never wedge the loop. Rolls up automation.goal-wait.

title: Send a message to any configured channel from a script, with no model call
contract: `hermes send [-t platform[:chat[:thread]]] [-f PATH|-] [-s SUBJECT] [-l] [--json] [message]` reuses the gateway's own platform credentials, resolves the body from argument / file / piped stdin, supports `MEDIA:<path>` attachments and `--list` target discovery, returns 0/1/2 exit codes, and needs **no running gateway** for bot-token platforms. Its own rebuild note calls it 'the single most useful automation primitive an agent framework can ship'. Rolls up automation.send.
governance: A reply into a live conversation thread is `channel.reply` (already KERNEL). A bare outbound send to the owner's own configured home channel is the reversible tier — but it must still be recorded in the IntentLog via audit_sink.py, or a script gains an unlogged voice as Nerva.
remaining_verbatim: Atașamentele `MEDIA:<path>` nu sunt purtate: o rută care citește căi locale și le trimite pe un canal e egress de fișiere și trebuie să ajungă în spatele Action Kernel-ului, cu un director-sursă delimitat, înainte să existe. Cerința structurală „fără gateway pornit” rămâne o divergență documentată: `nerva send` trece prin hub ca să existe IntentLog și rate-limit. Corpurile peste 4.000 de caractere sunt refuzate, nu fragmentate (Hermes fragmentează per platformă). Slack și Discord rămân reply-only (restul H018); email-ul e exclus deliberat. Nu există adresare `platform:chat_id[:thread]` / `platform:#canal` ca la Hermes: `--channel telegram` înseamnă întotdeauna chat-ul owner-ului. Precedența diverge deliberat: la Hermes argumentul câștigă în fața `--file`, aici ambele deodată e eroare de utilizare. Erorile nu au prefixul `hermes send:`. `JobRunner._send` își păstrează propria rezolvare a destinației (lot-ul jobs). Fără probă live pe un canal real din această sesiune: verificarea a fost prin hub fals și prin ChannelManager-ul real cu adaptoare false.
